channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Petistas acusam ACM Neto de imitar campanha de Lula; veja foto
item.description: PT members accused ACM Neto's campaign of copying visual elements from Lula's 2026 World Cup-themed campaign clip. Neto launched the jingle 'Dalê' with singer O Poeta in a baiano pagode style as part of his Bahia gubernatorial pre-campaign. Neto's team denied the allegations, stating the material is original and based on widely used graphic resources.

item.title: Flávio diz aguardar Michelle em sua campanha: “No tempo dela”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, presidential pre-candidate, stated he is waiting for Michelle Bolsonaro to join his campaign 'in her own time', emphasizing they share the same view of the federal government and believe 'no one can endure 4 more years of PT'. He stressed the need for unity to combat what he called 'Brazil's enemy' — the current government. Their strained relationship, already public for months, flared after a June 24 Instagram video in which Michelle said Flávio harshly criticized her on the phone for opposing the PL’s talks with Ciro Gomes in Ceará, telling her to stay out of party decisions, leading to her resignation from PL Women’s presidency.

item.title: Pesquisa sobre engajamento acende alerta para um dos candidatos ao Planalto
item.description: A VEJA em Foco survey revealed that Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) ranks last among presidential pre-candidates in social media follower growth and engagement rate, gaining only 67 new followers and showing declining interaction. Alek Maracajá, CEO of Ativaweb, warned this signals a campaign risk, as social media serve as a key political barometer. Meanwhile, Renan Santos (Missão) led growth with 24,080 new followers, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

item.title: Partidos acionam Justiça Eleitoral contra Rosângela Moro
item.description: PT, PCdoB and PV filed a representation with the TRE-PR against the mayor of Santo Antônio do Sudoeste (PR), Ricardo Antonio Ortina (PL), and pre-candidate Rosângela Moro (PL), accusing them of improper use of public resources to promote an electoral event. The parties claim the mayor used the official office, government flags and institutional setting to record and distribute an invitation in favor of Moro’s state deputy candidacy, undermining electoral equality. The Brazil of Hope Federation requested an injunction for immediate content removal, ban on similar future posts, and fines and sanctions.

item.title: Subvenção à gasolina é eleitoreira e deve ser retirada
item.description: The R$ 0.44 per liter gasoline subsidy is described as an electioneering measure that should be withdrawn, despite Iran-U.S. tensions and the approaching 2026 elections. Finance Minister Dario Durigan says the government plans to revive discussions to end the subsidy, which costs R$ 1.2 billion monthly and mainly benefits middle- and high-income groups and Petrobras. Lula had previously promised economic officials he would have authority to end the program when no longer needed, but re-election prospects may block the move.

item.title: Senado pode votar nova ‘pauta-bomba’ antes do recesso
item.description: The Senate may vote in first turn on a PEC granting differentiated retirement for community health agents and endemic disease combat agents before the recess, with an estimated cost of 69 billion reais. The bill, already in its fourth discussion session, could be voted on Tuesday the 14th, the date of its fifth and final mandatory session. The Planalto labels the proposal a 'budget bomb' due to its impact on pension regimes, creating an additional deficit of 28 billion reais and increasing spending by 24 billion reais over the next ten years.

item.title: Entidades do setor produtivo do Brasil e dos EUA propõem nova rodada de negociação para evitar tarifaço
item.description: The National Confederation of Industry (CNI), Amcham Brasil, and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce have urged a new round of negotiations between Brazil and the U.S. to avoid a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, which the U.S. claims stems from trade-restrictive practices. The U.S. government’s decision deadline is July 15, and Brazil’s foreign ministry has identified over 40 American companies at risk. The groups advocate a two-step approach: first addressing immediate trade issues, then expanding to long-term strategic economic cooperation.

item.title: Lula se reúne com o MST para discutir auxílio à Venezuela
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with MST representatives at the Palácio da Alvorada to discuss humanitarian aid for Venezuela, which was struck by a double earthquake on June 24. The Brazilian government has already sent six planes carrying medicines, water purifiers, field hospital supplies, food, military firefighters, search dogs, and trauma professionals. Attendees included MST national leader João Paulo Rodrigues and national coordinator João Pedro Stédile.

item.title: Direita tenta adiar PL das big techs para depois da eleição
item.description: Right-wing lawmakers in Brazilmakers proposed delaying the analysis of the Digital Markets Bill until after the 2026 elections. The bill's rapporteur, Deputy Aliel Machado (PV), opposed the delay and urged a vote before the parliamentary recess. The legislation aims to regulate major tech platforms in Brazil.

item.title: “Não tem como continuar”, diz Romário sobre Ancelotti
item.description: Romário strongly criticized the continued presence of Carlo Ancelotti as head coach of the Brazilian national team following Brazil's elimination in the 2026 World Cup, stating he would tear up the coach's contract and calling the team's performance shameful. He questioned tactical decisions, particularly the substitution of Bruno Guimarães with Ederson at full-back, and accused the media of being lenient toward foreign coaches. Romário also condemned the CBF for renewing Ancelotti's contract before the tournament ended, arguing it ensures a cycle of inconsistency and failure.

item.title: “O lance do Flávio é ficar rico e comprar imóveis”, diz Renan
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Renan Santos accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of having no interest in becoming president, only seeking to get rich and buy real estate. He also criticized the Novo party in an interview with MyNews.

item.title: A reação de Marina a Tarcísio por crítica sobre disputar eleição em São Paulo
item.description: Marina Silva criticized Tarcísio de Freitas for questioning her Senate candidacy in São Paulo, accusing him of applying 'double standards' and arrogance by claiming that generosity and hospitality should be monopolized by his political group. She emphasized her decades-long ties to the state, including being married to a São Paulo native for nearly 40 years, family connections in Santos since 1979, and receiving the title of 'Paulista citizen' in 1995, and suggested the criticism reflects resistance to women's presence in positions of power.

item.title: PL Mulher anuncia mudança e diz que Michelle Bolsonaro "não vai parar"
item.description: The social media team of PL Mulher announced it will step down from managing the profile starting next week, handing over command to a new team as directed by the party's national leadership. Despite the change, they stated that Michelle Bolsonaro "will not stop", directing followers to the 'Michelle Bolsonaro will not stop,' redirecting followers to the 'Imparáveis MB' profile, a movement led by her. Her departure from the national leadership of PL Mulher on June 30 occurred amid a public crisis with her stepson and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, stemming from disagreements over electoral strategies in Ceará.

item.title: ‘Esperando o tempo que ela achar suficiente’, diz Flávio Bolsonaro em meio a crise com Michelle
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) said he is waiting for the time that former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) deems sufficient to join his presidential campaign, following a public dispute sparked by her criticism of the PL’s negotiations with Ciro Gomes in Ceará. The family rift exposed internal party divisions, prompting Michelle to step down as head of PL Women and casting doubt on her Senate candidacy in the Federal District. The party has called for a truce until the July 25 convention.

item.title: Aécio Neves diz que não disputará presidência e descarta nome do PSDB para o pleito
item.description: Aécio Neves (PSDB-MG) ruled out running for president in 2026 and stated that the PSDB will not launch its own candidacy, choosing instead to focus on strengthening the party and the federation with Cidadania ahead of the 2030 election. He advocated for supporting a centrist candidate in a potential runoff, rejecting both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, and has not yet decided whether to run for Senate in Minas Gerais.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Flávio Bolsonaro de ‘criminoso’: ‘Está em Brasília para fazer negócios'
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential pre-candidate for the Missão party, accused Flávio Bolsonaro of being a 'criminal' focused solely on making business in Brasília and buying real estate, citing his ties to figures linked to organized crime and arms trafficking. He also criticized the Novo party as a subordinate of Bolsonarism and rejected the label of 'third way', stating he aims to defeat both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula indica desembargador Sergio Torres Teixeira para o cargo de ministro do TST
item.description: President Lula nominated Appeals Court Judge Sergio Torres Teixeira from the 6th Regional Labor Court of Pernambuco for a ministerial position at the Superior Labor Court (TST), filling the vacancy left by the retirement of Dora Maria da Costa. The nomination was published in the Official Gazette and now awaits Senate Judiciary Committee review before a plenary vote.

item.title: Zema critica filho de Gilmar Mendes por influência na CBF e diz que 'mão do STF chega até na escalação da Seleção'
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president and former governor of Minas Gerais, accused Francisco Mendes, son of Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, of exerting undue influence on the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) through an IDP agreement granting him 84% of revenue and of influencing Neymar’s call-up to the national team. Zema also linked a 2024 decision by Gilmar Mendes that restored CBF leadership, claiming the 'hand of the STF reaches even the national team lineup,' and criticized what he calls Brazil’s 'untouchables' system.

item.title: Sem estrutura, Joaquim Barbosa deve desistir de disputa pelo Planalto
item.description: Retired Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa is expected to withdraw from the 2026 presidential race due to the lack of structure and electoral alliances in the Christian Democracy party, which nominated him. Although announced as a candidate after Aldo Rebelo stepped aside, Barbosa never made public statements and awaited campaign guarantees that were not fulfilled. His withdrawal is expected to be formalized by August 5, the deadline for party conventions to define candidacies.

item.title: Publicitário alvo da PF foi responsável por apresentar Flávio Bolsonaro a Vorcaro
item.description: Publicist Thiago Miranda, targeted in a Federal Police operation, was responsible for introducing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to banker Daniel Vorcaro in 2024 and intermediating R$134 million in payments to a U.S.-based fund linked to a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Investigations also allege Miranda coordinated influencer campaigns against the Central Bank and gathered confidential data on journalists, with suspicions that funds were diverted to support Eduardo Bolsonaro’s stay in the United States.

item.title: Eleições 2026: federação entre PP e União Brasil deve retirar apoio a Flávio? Entenda
item.description: The federation between PP and União Brasil may lead to withdrawing support for Flávio Dino in the 2026 elections, due to ideological and strategic differences within the governing coalition. This move reflects efforts to realign center-right forces into a unified alternative against the PT. The decision remains pending internal negotiations and electoral viability assessments.

item.title: PT amplia papel de Alckmin no interior paulista
item.description: The PT has decided to increase the involvement of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin in political articulation in the interior of São Paulo, due to unfavorable numbers for the party in the region. The strategy aims to narrow the gap between Fernando Haddad and Tarcísio de Freitas in the race for state governor and strengthen Lula’s re-election bid against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Sobre crise com Michelle, Flávio Bolsonaro diz estar 'aberto a conversar' e espera 'o tempo que ela achar suficiente' para entrar na campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said he is 'open to talking' with Michelle Bolsonaro after their public fallout, waiting for her to decide when she’s ready to rejoin the campaign. He emphasized unity against the PT as a national priority, while PL leader Valdemar Costa Neto urges reconciliation before the party’s July 25 convention. The family rift exposes internal party divisions over Ceará strategy and Flávio’s candidacy.

item.title: Federação União-PP avalia ficar neutra na eleição nacional, fragilizando apoios a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The União Progressista federation is considering national neutrality in the 2026 presidential election, which could weaken support for Flávio Bolsonaro as a pre-candidate. This move is driven by factors such as the arrest of Márcio Canella, a Flávio-aligned União Brasil figure, and internal dissatisfaction over Flávio’s lack of support for Ciro Nogueira (PP), who is under PF investigation. Neutrality aims to ease state-level alliances and grant autonomy to local candidates.

item.title: Nova pesquisa Quaest mostra disputa Lula x Flávio após vídeo de Michelle e caso Jaques Wagner
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll registered at the TSE on April 9, 2026, will measure the presidential race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, covering topics such as Michelle Bolsonaro’s video and the investigation into Jaques Wagner and Banco Master. The previous survey from June 10 showed Lula at 44% and Flávio at 38% in a potential runoff, with a 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Ministros divergem sobre restrições da pré-campanha e aplicação da lei vira ‘barata-voa’ no Planalto
item.description: Lula government ministers are avoiding social media posts and interviews due to uncertainty about electoral law restrictions during the 'defeso eleitoral', with reported divergences between the AGU and the SAJ on permissible actions. Despite the AGU chief denying conflicts, officials describe inconsistent guidance, leading to content removals and changes in official messaging, including slogan replacements and the use of the national flag.

item.title: Conta do PL Mulher diz que ‘Michelle não vai parar’ em comunicado sobre reestruturação após saída da ex-primeira-dama
item.description: The official PL Mulher account announced its restructuring following Michelle Bolsonaro's departure as president of the party's women's wing, stating it will now be managed by a new team with its own methodology and agenda, in line with national PL leadership directives. Despite the change, the message pays tribute to Michelle, declaring 'Michelle will not stop' and emphasizing her legacy, claiming that thousands of women and men of good character are now 'unstoppable' and inviting followers to join the new movement she is said to lead.

item.title: Boulos diz que Trump interferiu na Copa e chama Flávio de “bajulador”
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) accused Donald Trump of interfering in the 2026 World Cup through calls to FIFA and restrictions on referees and players, calling such actions a threat to national sovereignty. He also criticized the Bolsonaro family, labeling Flávio Bolsonaro a 'sycophant' and suggesting Eduardo Bolsonaro ('bananinha') and Flávio act in U.S. interests, not Brazil's.

item.title: Se PL lançar Medioli em MG, Cleitinho ficará independente, diz Republicanos
item.description: The PL in Minas Gerais is considering launching Vittorio Medioli as its own candidate for state governor due to Cleitinho's (Republicanos) delay in defining his candidacy, aiming to create two electoral bases for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Republicanos stated that if the PL fields its own candidate, it will support Cleitinho independently, with a decision expected by August 5. The PL, holding its convention on July 23, sees Medioli as an alternative to strengthen support for presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Em ligação com Lula, Petro diz que garante transição pacífica na Colômbia
item.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro, in a call with Lula, affirmed his commitment to a peaceful transition in Colombia despite not recognizing the election victory of Abelardo de la Espriella. Petro reiterated his dedication to democracy and highlighted bilateral cooperation with Brazil, particularly on regional integration, Amazon preservation, and counter-narcotics efforts. Lula thanked Petro for the friendship and collaboration between the two nations during their overlapping presidencies.

item.title: Em meio a crise de transição na Colômbia, Lula e Petro conversam por telefone
item.description: Lula and Gustavo Petro spoke by phone regarding Colombia's transition crisis, in which Petro confirmed he will leave office on August 6, despite refusing to recognize the legitimacy of the election that elected Abelardo de la Espriella. Lula thanked Petro for their friendship and cooperation, noting his five visits to Colombia during their overlapping presidencies. Petro reaffirmed his commitment to democracy and a peaceful transition, even as he alleges fraud and calls for protests.

item.title: Pressão da Petrobras fez Casa Civil adiar Conselho de Política Energética
item.description: Petrobras pressured the federal government to postpone the National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) meeting for the fourth time in under two months, citing a shift in the Middle East war. The postponement, issued less than two hours before the scheduled July 8, 2026 meeting, came from the Civil House and was followed by the Ministry of Mines and Energy. Two key issues await CNPE deliberation: raising the mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline from E30 to E32 and auctioning the Union’s pre-sal natural gas share directly to the market — both contrary to Petrobras’ interests.

item.title: Ex-ministro de Bolsonaro diz que Flávio foi “omisso” com Michelle
item.description: Former minister Ricardo Salles accused Flávio Bolsonaro of remaining silent in the face of attacks by Bolsonarist allies of his brothers Carlos and Eduardo against Michelle Bolsonaro, claiming the senator failed to intervene. Salles stated that Michelle’s video was a justified response to months of accumulated hostility, even if the timing of its release could be debated.

item.title: Sob pressão
item.description: In 2025, Brazil officially halted fuel exports to Israel following sustained pressure from activists, unions, and UN rapporteurs. Although Petrobras claimed to have suspended sales since October 2023, data reveals Brazil became the fourth-largest crude oil supplier to Israel in 2024, exporting 2.9 million barrels — a 51% increase from 2023 — amid deepening diplomatic tensions over Lula’s pro-Palestine stance. The BDS Brazil campaign, supported by labor federations and human rights groups, was instrumental in ending the trade, reversing a surge that began under Bolsonaro, when exports peaked at 11.9 million barrels in 2022.

item.title: Pura encenação
item.description: The U.S. hearings on tariffs against Brazil confirmed expectations of additional import duties, with up to 37.5% on 35.2% of Brazil’s export basket to the U.S. Key sectors like pig iron, which supplies over 60% of U.S. imports, were highlighted as vulnerable, though exceptions were retained for critical inputs such as crude oil and green coffee. Brazilian representatives argued that tariffs would harm U.S. industry too, but no major shifts in position emerged during the two-day session.

item.title: O inferno astral dos Bolsonaro
item.description: The Bolsonaro family is facing an internal crisis that threatens their political project, with revelations of illegal funding requests by Flávio Bolsonaro and a public video by stepmother Michelle exposing strategic divisions. These events undermine the family unity that is the core of Bolsonarism, damaging both Flávio’s candidacy and Michelle’s prospects as an alternative leader within the clan.

item.title: Do asfalto às urnas
item.description: JR Freitas, a former app delivery worker and labor rights activist, is running for a seat in the São Paulo State Assembly in 2026 under the PSOL party. After leading worker strikes, sharing a stage with Lula, and winning legal battles against right-wing figures like Renan Santos, he has become a prominent critic of performative entrepreneurship and advocate for better working conditions for delivery workers. His trajectory combines online activism, federal task force participation, and involvement in drafting Bill 2479/25 to regulate the profession.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro é aconselhado a lançar mãe ao Senado pelo Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is being advised to nominate his mother, Rogéria Bolsonaro (PL), as a Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro in 2026. The information was reported in a subscriber-only article, suggesting a potential familial succession strategy within the Bolsonaro clan to maintain political influence in the state.

item.title: Flávio diz aguardar Michelle na campanha: ‘Esperando o tempo que ela achar que é o suficiente’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said he is waiting for Michelle Bolsonaro to decide whether to join his presidential campaign, stating he believes she thinks like him and that uniting against the Lula government is essential. He spoke after returning from a trip to the U.S., where his participation in a hearing was deemed awkward by private business representatives. The uncertainty around Michelle’s support concerns his campaign, particularly given his weak performance among female voters compared to Lula.

item.title: A nova pesquisa presidencial da Quaest
item.description: Quaest is conducting an in-person survey of 2,004 Brazilians from Friday to Monday to measure voting intentions for the presidency, with results scheduled for release on Wednesday, the 15th. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Zema mira o agro em anúncios
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) is running paid social media ads targeting agribusiness voters in Mato Grosso and Pará, highlighting record agricultural performance during his tenure as governor of Minas Gerais and promoting the slogan 'Agribusiness sustains Brazil. Now it's time for Brazil to sustain agribusiness'. He also criticizes the federal government and uses the slogan 'No more untouchables' in his presidential pre-campaign.

item.title: Aécio desiste de disputar a Presidência, e PSDB ficará sem candidato ao Planalto
item.description: Aécio Neves, national president of the PSDB, announced he will not run for President of Brazil in 2026. He stated that the party will not have a candidate in the presidential race, leaving the PSDB without a presidential contender in the October elections.

item.title: Projeto na Câmara proíbe atletas que jogam fora do Brasil e técnico estrangeiro na Seleção
item.description: Deputy Luiz Carlos Hauly (Podemos-PR) introduced a bill in the Chamber of Deputies that would ban the selection of Brazilian national team players who play abroad and foreign coaches, requiring all players and technical staff to be Brazilian nationals linked to clubs based in Brazil. The bill also prohibits sports betting and gambling sponsorships for sports entities, with penalties including loss of public funds and tax incentives. The proposal came shortly after Brazil’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup, while current head coach Carlo Ancelotti, an Italian, remains under contract with the CBF until 2030.

item.title: Canella contrata ex-advogado de Vorcaro para defendê-lo
item.description: The former mayor of Belford Roxo and Senate pre-candidate Márcio Canella (União Brasil), arrested in the PF's Unha e Carne operation for allegedly being the political arm of a criminal organization suspected of laundering R$ 7.6 billion through a Rio de Janeiro fuel station network, has hired lawyer Pierpaolo Bottini for his defense. The exclusive subscriber-only article underscores the connection between his case and ongoing investigations into corruption and money laundering.

item.title: ‘Apostar faz você perder dinheiro’: como o governo Lula vai endurecer a publicidade de bets
item.description: The Lula government will announce new rules for sports betting advertising, requiring warnings such as 'Betting makes you lose money' in all ads and prohibiting ads that portray betting as an investment or financial solution. Measures include fines of up to 20% of revenue, license suspensions, and cracking down on over 56,000 illegal betting sites already shut down.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TSE apresenta legislação eleitoral para candidatas
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) presented electoral legislation during the 'Course for Electoral Candidates – Brazil Edition', organized by the OEA, OEA School of Government, and Anadep, focusing on political violence against women and campaign financing. Judge Graciela de Rezende Henriquez emphasized Law No. 14.192/2021, which defines political violence against women as any action aimed at preventing, hindering, or restricting their political rights. The course aimed to train women for participation in the 2026 General Elections.

item.title: Aécio Neves desiste de candidatura e diz que PSDB não lançará nome ao Planalto
item.description: Aécio Neves withdrew his pre-candidacy for president in 2026 and announced that the PSDB will not launch any candidate for the Planalto, nor support others at this time. Despite running in 2014 with 48.36% of the vote, recent polls show him at only 2%, reflecting his inability to break through the Lula-Bolsonaro polarization. The party may consider supporting a centrist candidate in the first round but will remain neutral in the second.

item.title: A estratégia do PT para derrotar Ciro Gomes no Ceará
item.description: Governor Elmano de Freitas's campaign in Ceará relies on Lula's expected support to overcome Ciro Gomes' initial lead in polls, trusting in the Workers' Party's historical strength in the state. The strategy involves strengthening the ticket with allies like Camilo Santana and Cid Gomes, and negotiating the inclusion of centrist parties in the coalition, with key positions such as vice-governor and Senate candidates still to be defined.

item.title: ‘Sou corinthiana, não flamenguista’: Tebet rebate crítica de Tarcísio por não ser de SP
item.description: Simone Tebet rebutted Tarcísio de Freitas' criticism about her political origins, stating she is a Corinthians fan, pays taxes in São Paulo for ten years, and did not need to use a false address to run. She noted that Tarcísio, a Rio native and Flamengo supporter, also changed his electoral domicile to SP in 2022. Marina Silva also responded, accusing the governor of gender bias and double standards.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro volta ao Brasil, diz estar aberto ao diálogo e espera apoio de Michelle: 'Pensa igual a mim'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL-RJ pre-candidate for presidency, said he is open to dialogue and waiting for the right time for Michelle Bolsonaro’s support, stating she 'thinks like me'. He emphasized the need for right-wing unity to defeat the PT in the 2026 elections, following a conflict that began over disagreements on the Ceará Senate seat and escalated after Michelle released a critical video and stepped down from PL Women’s leadership. PL president Valdemar Costa Neto also urged unity, saying he will work personally to reconcile the two.
